warnings: This is a biostimulant study with protein hydrolysates, not CO2 enrichment
Multiple treatment combinations including FPH alone, NPK alone, and FPH+NPK combinations
Two different crops with different experimental setups
Control is T1 'Without fertilizer (control)' - no biostimulant application
Risk of confusing NPK-only treatments with control
Different FPH products used for each crop (FPH-160 for mung bean, FPH-180 for patchouli)

recon.variance_source: Table 5: 'Mean values ±standard errors for plant height, number of leaves, leaf area, and SPAD value of patchouli plants' and Table 6: 'Mean values ±standard errors for plant height, number of trifoliate leaves, and SPAD value of mung bean'
recon.control_definition: T1: Without fertilizer (control) - no biostimulant or fertilizer application
recon.treatment_definition: Various FPH (feather protein hydrolysate) concentrations (0.5-5 mL/L) alone or combined with 50% NPK
recon.potential_tc_confusion: NPK-only treatments (T8, T16) are NOT controls - they are mineral fertilizer treatments
recon.sample_size_source: The experiment was arranged in a randomized block design with 16 treatments. There were two replicates of each treatment arranged within two blocks
recon.extraction_guidance: Extract yield data from Table 7 (mung bean yield per plant in g) and Figure 2 (patchouli dry weight in g). Control is always T1. For biostimulant treatments, extract T2-T7 (FPH alone) and T9-T14 (FPH+NPK combinations) vs T1 control. Do NOT use T8 or T16 as controls - these are NPK fertilizer treatments. Standard errors are provided. Note very low sample size (n=2) which may affect statistical reliability.
